content.title: Sean Penn Is a No-Show at the 2026 Oscars for His Third Win, Presenter Kieran Culkin Jokes He 'Didn't Want to' Be Here
content.text: Sean Penn won his third Academy Award and first in the best supporting actor category for playing Col. Steven J. Lockjaw in 'One Battle After Another' Published on March 15, 2026 08:37PM EDT Sean Penn in 'One Battle After Another'. Credit : Warner Bros. NEED TO KNOW Sean Penn won best supporting actor at the 2026 Oscars for his role as Col. Steven J. Lockjaw in One Battle After AnotherIt is Penn's third Oscar, having previously won best actor for 'Mystic River' in 2004 and 'Milk' in 2009Kieran Culkin accepted the award for Penn, who was not in attendance, saying the actor "couldn't be here this evening, or didn't want to" Sean Penn won his third Academy Award at the 2026 Oscars on Sunday night. The actor was not on hand, however, to take home the best supporting actor award for his work as the ill-fated villain Col. Steven J. Lockjaw in Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another because he is currently out of the country. Kieran Culkin, who won the same category for his work in A Real Pain last year, accepted the award on the actor's behalf, saying: "Sean Penn couldn't be here this evening, or didn't want to, so I'll be accepting the award on his behalf." Penn previously took home the Best Actor Oscar for his work in Mystic River in 2004 and Milk in 2009. He was also nominated in the best actor category for his work in Dead Man Walking, Sweet and Lowdown and I Am Sam. Sean Penn as Col. Steven J Lockjaw in 'One Battle After Another'. Warner Bros. The actor had previously won best supporting actor at the BAFTA Film Awards and Actor Awards in February, but was also absent from those ceremonies. This year's best supporting actor category pitted Penn against three beloved industry veterans and one of Hollywood's hottest young stars. Penn beat out his One Battle After Another castmate Benecio del Toro, Sentimental Value star Stellan Skarsgård, Delroy Lindo of Sinners and Jacob Elordi, who played the title charcater in Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein. Penn did attend the Golden Globe Awards back in January, but lost out in the best supporting actor category to Skarsgard. The actor previously admitted to dragging his feet when it came to reading the script for One Battle After Another, which marked his second collaboration with Anderson after his role in he director's previous film, Licorice Pizza. "I came out of a shower late one night, and I was just walking to get dressed, and I had the script sitting there, and I thought, 'Okay, I'll read just one page,'" Penn told Entertainment Weekly back in September. He continued: "And I started to read, and I don't know, half a page, a page in, I'm sitting there dripping naked on the floor reading a script until I drip-dried and finished it."
